To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the structure reveals how AMPK is activated in response to cellular stress, 2) the structure shows how the AMPK activator ZMP is bound to the regulatory subunit, 3) the structure provides a basis for understanding how the AMPK regulatory subunit is regulated, and 4) the structure provides the basis for designing AMPK activators and inhibitors.
AMPK is a heterotrimeric kinase with a catalytic alpha subunit and a regulatory beta and gamma subunit and that the gamma subunit contains CBS domains that bind AMP and ATP to activate the kinase.
the structure of the CBS-domain pair of the regulatory gamma subunits of AMPK in complex of AMP and ZMP reveals a novel mechanism of allosteric regulation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure, function and regulation of proteins involved in energy metabolism.
the structure, function and regulation of AMPK, a central metabolic regulator in eukaryotes, and the structure, function, and regulation of the cystathionine beta synthase (CBS) family of enzymes.
the structure and function of AMPK, the central regulator of energy homeostasis in mammalian cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structure is not consistent with the proposed allosteric mechanism of activation of AMPK by ZMP.
the structure of the AMPK gamma1 CBS-domain pair in complex with AMP/ZMP provides a molecular framework for understanding how the binding of AMP and ZMP activates AMPK.
the crystal structures of CBS domain pairs from the AMPK regulatory subunits of different origins, including the human AMPK gamma 1, gamma 2, and gamma 3 subunits, have been solved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the structure of a CBS pair in AMPK is similar to that of a CBS pair of a human homologue of the yeast protein Gtr1p (a GTPase activating protein for Ras-related protein Rho1), and that AMP and ZMP bind in a similar way to the two CBS domains.
we have solved a high-resolution structure of a CBS domain pair in complex with two different ligands.
the AMPK structure is very similar to the structure of human CBS, with the exception that the active site of the gamma1 CBS-domain pair has a different orientation relative to the rest of the domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binding sites for AMP and ZMP are not identical.
AMP and ZMP bind in a similar fashion, with ZMP binding more tightly than AMP, and that ZMP is a better activator than AMP.
the two CBS domains of AMPK are structurally distinct and have different affinities for the activators.
